description.narrative:
The IJR works with the broad goal to build of societies that are fair, inclusive, democratic, and peaceful - in contexts that are currently afflicted by conflict or where societies continue to grapple with the historical legacy of such conflicts. Towards meeting this objective, IJR works with three key outcome areas:
- Policy actors use peace building and governance research in policy processes. - Communities demonstrating agency in transforming relations in divided communities - Stakeholders implement transitional justice policies, programs, and processes.

The Institute for Justice and Reconciliation (IJR) har begärt kärnstöd för genomförande av sitt program under strategiperioden 2021-2025. IJR är sedan tidigare en partnerorganisation till Sida, vilket inkluderar de senaste två strategiperioderna, och arbetar för rättvisa, inkluderande, demokratiska och fredliga samhällen i Afrika genom arbeta fram relevanta interventioner som kombinerar forskning, dialog, kapacitetsbyggande, opinionsbildning, policyrådgivning samt stöd till genomförande.
IJR arbetar utifrån ett brett mål om att bygga rättvisa, inkluderande, demokratiska och fredliga samhällen i kontexter påverkade av rådande konflikter eller där samhällen fortsätter att kämpa med det historiska arvet från tidigare sådana konflikter. IJR arbetar med fem nyckelområden, vilka inkluderar:
- Deltagare har förmåga att använda mekanismer för övergångsrättvisa som är kontextuellt lämpliga
- Deltagare är motiverade att möjliggöra rättvisa, inkludering och fred
- Deltagare vidtar åtgärder som leder till upprätthållen fred, rättvisa och försoning
- Samhällen är mer motståndskraftiga, försonade och socialt sammanhållda.
- System och policyer bidrar till realiseringen av rättvisa, inkluderande, demokratiska och fredliga samhällen.
IJR kommer att arbeta med fem tematiska områden vilka fokuserar på social sammanhållning, inkludering och antirasism; främja mänsklig värdighet och försoning på lokal nivå, övergångsrättvisa centrerad kring överlevare; socioekonomisk rättvisa och inkluderande utveckling samt gränsöverskridande dialog och regional försoning.

The Institute for Justice and Reconciliation (IJR) has requested for core support towards implementing its programmes under the strategy period form 2021 - 2025. IJR has been partnering with Sida in the past including the last two strategy periods and it is working towards fair, inclusive, democratic, and peaceful societies in Africa by designing relevant interventions combining research, dialogue, capacity building, advocacy, policy advice and implementation support.
The IJR works with the broad goal to build of societies that are fair, inclusive, democratic and peaceful - in contexts that are currently afflicted by conflict or where societies continue to grapple with the historical legacy of such conflicts. IJR works with five key outcome areas including:
- Participants have the capacity to use contextually appropriate transitional justice mechanisms
- Participants are motivated to enable fairness, inclusivity and peace
- Participants take actions that lead to sustained peace, justice and reconciliation
- Communities are more resilient, reconciled and socially cohesive
- Systems and policies enable the realisation of fair, inclusive, democratic and peaceful societies
IJR will work on five thematic areas that focuses on social cohesion, inclusion and anti-racism; advancing human dignity and bottom-up reconciliation; survivor-centred transitional justice and reconciliation; socio-economic justice and inclusive development; and cross-border dialogue and regional reconciliation.

description.narrative:
The key achievement reported for 2024 include expanding engagement with the United Nations, African Union, and regional bodies. Notable engagements included input on transforming the UN Security Council, the Summit of the Future, Review of the UN Peace building Architecture and contributions to the Women, Peace, and Security Agenda. Regionally, the Data4Governance Project worked in support of the African Governance Architecture, whilst the support for the Peace and Security Council, C-PAPS and RECs on transitional justice, peace and security and women peace and security continued. IJR also continued to work with civil society across the continent hosting many regional seminars. IJR conducted various activities that have all been part of trying to meet the objectives of creating spaces and interventions that promote justice, reconciliation and social cohesion and an informed and engaged citizenry; as well as supporting the implementation of frameworks, policies and processes that lead to more peaceful and just societies. These all speak to meeting IJRs overall 3 Outcomes which are:
1. Policy actors using peace building and governance research in policy processes.
In 2024, the Research and Policy Unit provided empirical data and analysis to inform decision-making and advocacy efforts that included:
- Completion of Afrobarometer Round 9 surveys in Lesotho and Botswana. - Produced a South African Reconciliation Barometer (SARB) report, informing key stakeholders on public perceptions of social cohesion. - Engagement with regional and global think tanks to provide policy recommendations on governance and reconciliation.
2. Communities demonstrating agency in transforming relations in divided communities.
The Sustained Dialogues Program amplified community voices through local-level dialogues and workshops. In 2024, the program supported community-led initiatives tackling issues of democracy, voting rights, gender identity, and conflict resolution. The dialogues focused on creating safe spaces for discussions on South Africas past, racial identity, respect, and social cohesion. Trauma healing and reconciliation efforts were also a key focus of the programme.
3. Stakeholders implement transitional justice policies, programs, and processes.
in 20254, the Peace building Programme focused on fostering dialogue, mediation, and policy engagement across conflict-affected areas.
Key activities included:
- Capacity-building interventions in Ghana, Kenya, and Ethiopia to strengthen peace processes. - Supporting Sudans Transitional Justice Expert Group, contributing to national reconciliation efforts. - Engagements in Burundi and Zimbabwe, focusing on cross-border conflict resolution and mediation practices. - Hosting a regional authors' workshop on Preventing Violent Extremism (PVE) in Addis Ababa. - Womens Election Mechanism for Peace WEMP was deployed in five provinces, training 300 peace monitors and establishing peace rooms. The initiative strengthened womens participation in electoral processes and contributed to conflict prevention during elections. The projects impact will be further assessed to determine best practices for scaling similar interventions in future elections.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
